question:
The man is being held captive by a kidnapper. On a smartphone call, the kidnapper lets him (or makes him) hear the ransom demand directed at his daughter: bring 100 million yen alone by noon tomorrow, or the hostage—the father—will die. The daughter, hearing her father's plight, is the one being told to deliver the money and pleads with the kidnapper to spare her father's life.

Overhearing the call, the father realizes the danger is aimed at his daughter: to deliver the money alone, she would have to come to the kidnapper, who intends to kill her when she arrives (to eliminate the witness). The father also infers this from the kidnapper's words during the call. Since he is able to speak on the call, the father tells his daughter that the ransom should not be paid. He is willing to accept that the kidnapper, denied the money, may kill him—he would rather die himself than have his daughter walk into the trap and be killed. That is why, hearing the demand, he decides the ransom should not be paid: to protect his daughter's life, even at the cost of his own.
